articles.title: Pentagon No. 3 frustrates senators in closed-door briefing on Iran war, Trump defense strategy
articles.summary: Democratic and Republican lawmakers alike emerged Thursday from a closed-door briefing frustrated by what they said was a lack of clear answers from Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby on the Trump administration’s National Defense Strategy and the ongoing Iran war. The briefing with the Senate Armed Services Committee started off rocky, with Colby immediately opening…
articles.body:
Democratic and Republican lawmakers alike emerged Thursday from a closed-door briefing frustrated by what they said was a lack of clear answers from Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby on the Trump administration’s National Defense Strategy and the ongoing Iran war.

The briefing with the Senate Armed Services Committee started off rocky, with Colby immediately opening the floor for questions without first giving an opening statement, Sen. Kevin Cramer (R-N.D.) told The Hill.

“There were a lot more questions than answers,” Cramer said, noting that it was “very peculiar” and “weird” that Colby — at the Capitol to give lawmakers a congressionally mandated update — did not have a statement prepared.

Cramer also said the exchange seemed “very disrespectful to say the least” and was a “dodge and punt” on Colby’s part.

“You don’t have to go far in Congress to have a sort of confrontational view of Elbridge Colby, but boy, he just blew her up right from the beginning,” he said.

Sen. Joni Ernst (R-Iowa), likewise, said she was “very disappointed” by the briefing.

“I did not stay to ask questions because he was not giving any clear responses,” Ernst told The Hill.

Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) said Iran was the main focus of the gathering, even as it had been scheduled to discuss the National Defense Strategy.

But, “like a lot of the briefs we get from this administration, we walk out with more questions than we had when we went in,” he told reporters.

Senate Armed Services Committee Chair Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) and ranking member Jack Reed (D-R.I.) declined to comment.

Lawmakers have become exasperated over the Trump administration’s ongoing war in Iran, known as Operation Epic Fury, which has stretched into its seventh month with no clear end to the fighting.

President Trump, who initially predicted a swift victory that would come within weeks when the war began on Feb. 28, earlier this month said the deeply unpopular conflict that has sent energy prices soaring will likely last through the November midterm elections.

On Thursday, Trump told Axios he had “ a big decision coming up ” regarding Iran.

“Do I want to go in and annihilate them [the Iranian regime] or do I not? It’s a big decision. Anything could happen with me,” Trump said.

The president is slated to meet with the leaders of six Persian Gulf nations on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly next week.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.) offered a rare, positive view of Colby’s briefing, saying “he was very detailed and constructive” and “didn’t hide from any question, he answered every question with substance.”

Democratic lawmakers “are going to politicize these hearings no matter what,” Banks told The Hill.

Colby’s briefing came the same day all of the Senate Democratic Conference, minus John Fetterman (Pa.), signed a letter led by Sen. Elissa Slotkin (Mich.) pressing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for answers on the cost of the Iran war.

The lawmakers, which also include Independent Sens. Bernie Sanders (Vt.) and Angus King (Maine), demanded by the end of the month a detailed breakdown on the costs incurred since the start of the war, how the Trump administration’s supplemental request would be spent, and how some $34 billion in remaining funding from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act will be allocated.

“Despite asking for tens of billions of additional taxpayer dollars, you have so far failed to provide basic information on how this money has and will be spent,” according to the letter. “Congress must have access to this information to carry out our oversight responsibilities.”

The Pentagon told Congress last month that the cost of the Iran war has now climbed to more than $42 billion — a $4.5 billion increase to the most recent public estimate from the Defense Department.

The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office, meanwhile, earlier this week said the conflict could cost around $2 billion per month for as long as it continues.

Alexander Bolton and Helen Huiskes contributed.

articles.title: RFK Jr. says anti-vaccine group has a ‘friend at the White House’
articles.summary: Speaking to the anti-vaccine group he once led, Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said Thursday the Trump administration supports its cause. “You have a strong and steadfast friend at the White House,” Kennedy told dozens of attendees at a one-day conference put on by Children’s Health Defense, the organization he…
articles.body:
Speaking to the anti-vaccine group he once led, Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said Thursday the Trump administration supports its cause.

“You have a strong and steadfast friend at the White House,” Kennedy told dozens of attendees at a one-day conference put on by Children’s Health Defense, the organization he co-founded and led from 2015 to 2023.

Kennedy’s appearance at the conference highlighted how close he remains to the anti-vaccine movement, despite his efforts over the past year to appear to distance himself.

Thursday’s conference in Washington, D.C., marked Kennedy’s first appearance at an official Children’s Health Defense conference since he joined the Trump administration, but the group now wields significant political clout.

Kennedy did not attend the group’s national conference last year.

Leaders of the organization have been hired in prominent positions at the HHS, and views that were once considered fringe — like a false and debunked link between vaccines and autism — have become mainstream in the Trump administration, oftentimes echoed by President Trump himself.

In a speech that spanned more than an hour, Kennedy initially ran through his agency’s accomplishments to address chronic illness and promote healthier food. But he quickly turned to questioning the safety of routine vaccination.

Kennedy said Trump has tasked him to “vigorously investigate the potential contribution of childhood vaccines to the chronic disease epidemic.”

“The question is, should we be looking at the potential that some of these chronic illnesses are associated with vaccines?” Kennedy said.

He claimed that diabetes, sudden infant death syndrome and anorexia can be side effects of routine vaccines. Kennedy also vowed to investigate chemtrails and electromagnetic fields.

Kennedy urged patience with federal bureaucracy but assured the audience that change is happening.

“Over the past 19 months, we have fundamentally changed how the federal government responds to parents who question what they’ve been told about vaccines,” Kennedy said. “President Trump will not allow the government to treat parents who question vaccine orthodoxies as lepers … we have started asking the questions that you and millions of American parents have been asking for years, and the establishment has pushed back very hard.”

Kennedy said he had a mandate to shake up the Washington, D.C., establishment.

“I didn’t come to Washington to protect institutions from uncomfortable questions,” he said. “I came to make those institutions answer those questions, and I intend to stay in this fight as long as I am able.”

articles.body:
Maryland Gov. Wes Moore (D) said Thursday he would “absolutely sign” a statewide data center moratorium if brought to his desk, joining other governors and elected officials calling for a freeze on developing new data centers.

“If the statewide moratorium bill lands on your desk in 2027, would you sign it?” Punchbowl News’s Mikenzie Frost asked Moore in an interview .

“Yes,” Moore quickly said. “And here’s the thing, it’s like — I believe that local jurisdictions should have say and they should not be told nor dictated, and I do understand there are certain local jurisdictions who want it. I just need them to understand I have very strict guidelines of what’s going to actually get state approval and state authority.”

He added that if a bill approaches him, he “will absolutely sign it.”

Thirteen of the Old Line State’s 24 jurisdictions have implemented temporary bans on data center development. Among those jurisdictions are Baltimore, Worcester, Calvert, Montgomery and Prince George’s counties, the latter two of which border Washington, D.C.

Moore, who is facing reelection in November against former state Del. Dan Cox (R), has previously urged data centers in his state to bring their own energy resources and meet environmental regulations, largely leaving the power of what to do with data centers to local officials, Maryland Matters reported in August.

Residents from the counties putting these moratoriums in place have been vocal in their opposition to data center development and their impact on housing and utility costs.

At the federal level, Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) on Thursday blocked a Republican-led bill to have states consider requiring tech companies to cover increased electricity costs from their operations. He said it was not enough.

“Rather than voluntary pledges or suggestions to states, Congress needs to pass real legislation with real teeth,” Heinrich said.

Also on Thursday, New Mexico gubernatorial candidate Deb Haaland (D) announced that she backed a moratorium , emphasizing the environmental impact and keeping the environment safe. She called for requiring data centers to build their own renewable energy infrastructure to prevent New Mexicans from paying soaring energy costs.

New Mexico has 21 operational data centers, with one under construction, five planned, one paused and on inactive, according to the U.S. Data Center Map .

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott (R) on Monday directed the Texas Water Development Board to penalize data centers found not to enforce state requirements on water usage or face criminal consequences. Those centers would become ineligible to receive permits or renewals from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality.

President Trump has said data centers must pay for their own water and power consumption, an increasingly bipartisan position, but he slammed New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) in July for a statewide freeze on data center development.

“Data Centers are tremendous WINS for the States and Communities that are lucky enough to get them. New York should change its Policy, IMMEDIATELY,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “The Radical Left Dumocrats must not be allowed to cause us to lose Data Centers, AI, and all of this incredible new Technology, to China, and other countries!”

State Department OKs potential $24B fighter jet sale to Saudis

The State Department announced Thursday that it approved a potential $24 billion sale of F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia , despite worries from defense officials and lawmakers that China could acquire the plane’s technology.

The potential sale, which can still be paused by Congress, includes 48 F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter aircraft with conventional takeoff and landing and 49 Pratt & Whitney F135-PW-100 engines, the State Department said in a press release.

If the sale goes through, Saudi Arabia would become only the second country in the Middle East to operate the U.S. F-35s, apart from Israel.

Israel has long been against the Kingdom acquiring the fighter planes, worrying that the sale would alter the country’s so-called qualitative military edge (QME) , a regional superiority that Congress committed to follow in a 2008 law.

But the State Department said on Thursday the potential sale “ will not alter the military balance in the region.”

The sale would improve Saudi Arabia’s “ capability to deter current and future threats by strengthening its homeland defense, and improving interoperability with U.S. forces, and other regional and NATO forces,” the department said, adding the transaction would “ augment Saudi Arabia’s operational aircraft and enhance its air-to-air, and air-to-ground self-defense capability.”

The potential sale of the stealth aircraft – which is produced by Lockheed Martin and can gather intelligence and conduct long-range strike missions would present a major warfare upgrade for Saudi Arabia’s air force and could affect the balance of power in the Middle East, experts told The Hill last November .

Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.) urged the Trump administration not to move forward with the sale “ when our own intelligence community is warning that it could put the crown jewels of American military technology within reach of the Chinese Communist Party.”

“ Beijing has spent decades stealing American intellectual property and technology to close the gap with the United States, and we must not help them do it,” Krishnamoorthi wrote Thursday on the social platform X. “We must not sell our most advanced fighter jet anywhere the CCP may be able to get its hands on the technology inside it.”

The sale of the fighter jets, which Saudi Arabia has long sought , comes as the kingdom has come under fire from Iranian one-way attack drones and missiles since the start of the U.S. war against Iran and recent attacks from Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

articles.title: Pentagon issues new guidance for testosterone testing after rescinding previous one
articles.summary: The Pentagon issued new guidance late Thursday instructing mandatory testosterone deficiency screening for male active-duty and ​reserve service members over the age of 30 after temporarily rescinding previous guidance earlier this month. The department said the updated guidance will address male testosterone deficiency and establish uniform screening and treatment pathways across the Defense Health Agency…
articles.body:
The Pentagon issued new guidance late Thursday instructing mandatory testosterone deficiency screening for male active-duty and ​reserve service members over the age of 30 after temporarily rescinding previous guidance earlier this month.

The department said the updated guidance will address male testosterone deficiency and establish uniform screening and treatment pathways across the Defense Health Agency (DHA).

The Pentagon says this is being done so the U.S. military has a lethal fighting force “prepared to dominate the battlefield and achieve peace through strength.”

“By proactively identifying and treating suboptimal hormone levels, the Department continues to invest in the health of its warfighters, strengthen their performance and maximize force readiness,” Pentagon chief spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a statement .

The screening will consist of a “structured symptom and risk-factor assessment,” the DHA said, while male service members under the age of 30 will be screened on request or where “clinical indicators are identified by the examining provider.”

The DHA said the provider will document the presence or absence of each of the symptoms, along with risk factors.

Symptoms include erectile dysfunction, reduced sexual desire, unexplained loss of muscle mass or gain in fat, depressed mood, low motivation, disturbed sleep, impaired concentration or memory, diminished physical performance or endurance not correlated with injury and loss of spontaneous morning erections.

Risk factors include obesity, type two diabetes or metabolic syndrome, chronic opioid or glucocorticoid therapy, prior traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness, testicular trauma, torsion, undescended testis, orchitis or prior chemotherapy or pelvic radiation, known or suspected obstructive sleep apnea, low-trauma fracture, recurrent bone stress injury, unexplained anemia, infertility and gynecomastia, according to the DHA.

“The combination of reduced sexual desire, loss of spontaneous morning erections, and erectile dysfunction have been shown to be most specific for androgen deficiency,” the DHA said in the document. “The remaining symptoms are sensitive but nonspecific, and are more commonly attributable to sleep restriction, energy deficit, mood disorder, or overtraining.”

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled the Pentagon’s effort to screen service members’ testosterone levels and offer testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) in July, stating it would be a way to keep soldiers on the “leading edge of lethality.”

“While we invest heavily in our weapon systems, platforms and gear, our most decisive tactical advantage will always be the individual warfighter,” Hegseth said in a video at the time . “We have a sacred duty to maintain that advantage, which is why we must constantly look for new ways to optimize your performance, your resilience and your long-term health.”

The female clinical practice guideline is being reviewed and will be posted “upon approval,” Vice Adm. Darin K. Via, director of the DHA, said in a Thursday memo.

For male service members, the diagnosis will not be made after a first test, as the second test will be done on a different day under the same “pre-test conditions,” the guideline said.

Service members will be tested between 7 and 10 a.m., but for those on night or rotating shifts, they will be tested within three hours of waking up after a full night’s sleep. The service members will be tested while fasting and not within 30 days of recovery from being sick.

DHA will consider multiple formulations before offering TRT, including the service member’s preference and convenience when picking the type and dose, ability to comply with treatment and the appropriateness of the selected product.

“Injection therapy will consist of testosterone cypionate or enanthate, subcutaneous or intramuscular, with starting doses of 100 mg once weekly, or the weekly dose divided and administered twice weekly,” the DHA said in the guidance.

TRT can be initiated within 90 days of the service member’s deployment, but continuing during deployment will warrant a four-to-six-week follow-up assessment to show “clinical stability and a testosterone level within the target range of 300–600 ng/dL,” according to the DHA.

“Once stability has been established, the patient would then transition to the every-6-month monitoring schedule,” DHA said. “A Service member who is stable on testosterone therapy should be deployable without requiring a waiver, depending on the formulation.”

articles.title: Horse in New Mexico infected with screwworm before Mexico livestock imports resume
articles.summary: A new case of New World screwworm was confirmed in a horse in New Mexico Thursday, days before the state was set to resume livestock imports from Mexico. The infected horse was in Grant County near the Mexican border, according to the Department of Agriculture. It is the second confirmed case in New Mexico since…
articles.body:
A new case of New World screwworm was confirmed in a horse in New Mexico Thursday, days before the state was set to resume livestock imports from Mexico.

The infected horse was in Grant County near the Mexican border, according to the Department of Agriculture. It is the second confirmed case in New Mexico since the flesh-eating parasite entered the U.S. in June from Mexico.

The case comes after Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins announced that USDA was preparing to reopen the Santa Teresa port of entry to livestock from Mexico on Sept. 24.

According to the New Mexico Department of Agriculture, the horse’s infection had not yet been confirmed at the time of the announcement, which was made by Rollins at a news conference in Santa Teresa on Thursday.

The Trump administration halted livestock imports along the southern border last year in an effort to curb the spread of the New World screwworm. Imports resumed last month through a port in Arizona as part of a “phased reopening.”

The USDA has tracked 50 confirmed cases of screwworm in the U.S. since the first report of an outbreak occurred on June 3. As of Thursday, only three of those cases were still active, according to the department’s online dashboard .

Last month, four cases were reported, all in Texas. Of the two cases reported so far this month, one occurred in Texas, while the other was in New Mexico.

New World screwworm infestations occur when fly larvae enter an open wound and feed on the living tissue of warm-blooded animals. The parasite can kill animals if infestations are left untreated.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has characterized the risk to humans as “very low,” and there have not been any reports of human infestations.

articles.title: US Said to Hold Off on Tariffs Until After Xi-Trump Summit
articles.summary: The US is expected to hold off announcing new tariffs on China and other trading partners until after next week’s summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Do...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The US is expected to hold off announcing new tariffs on China and other trading partners until after next week's summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, according to people familiar with the matter, a delay that could preserve such a threat as leverage in the negotiations.

While the reason for the postponement is unclear, Trump has repeatedly used tariff warnings to press trading partners for concessions. The administration had intended to release a trade report on alleged excess capacity before the meeting that would recommend a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods, Bloomberg previously reported.

It's also uncertain whether the final tariff rate will change from the previously expected level, which would restore Trump's second-term duties on China to around 20%, which Beijing has previously said is consistent with its trade truce with Washington.

US and Chinese negotiators are set to meet over the weekend to discuss any agreements ahead of Xi's state visit. The trip would be Xi's first to the US since 2023, when he met former President Joe Biden during a visit that included attending the APEC summit in San Francisco.

In March, the Trump administration launched an investigation into more than a dozen major trading partners under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 over excess capacity concerns. Those expected levies, along with already-implemented duties related to forced labor, are set to eventually bring rates closer to Trump's country-specific tariffs that were overturned by the Supreme Court earlier this year.

The Office of the US Trade Representative and the White House did not respond to requests for comment. Inside US Trade first reported the delay.

China has previously signaled that it could take action if US tariffs exceed prevailing levels when the trade truce was struck.

"Capacity issues should be viewed in a comprehensive and fair manner, and should not be used as a pretext for protectionism," Huang Ling, a spokesperson for China's Ministry of Commerce, said in late August. "We will continue to closely follow and comprehensively assess subsequent US moves, and reserve the right to take all necessary measures."

articles.title: Bank of Japan hikes rates to 31-year high to battle inflation
articles.summary: The Bank of Japan raised interest rates to a 31-year high on Friday and said it would lift them further as it looks to counter inflation fuelled by surging e...
articles.body:
The Bank of Japan raised interest rates to a 31-year high on Friday and said it would lift them further as it looks to counter inflation fuelled by surging energy prices and a weak yen.

The 25-basis-point hike to 1.25 percent was expected by markets following the recent tightening by the European Central Bank and the US Federal Reserve, though the decision was not unanimous as it was carried by a 7-2 majority vote.

Pressure has increased on officials to further tighten monetary policy as a spike in oil prices caused by the Middle East crisis -- which shows little sign of ending anytime soon -- is expected to keep putting upward pressure on inflation.

"Given that underlying CPI inflation has been approaching two percent and financial conditions have been accommodative, the bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate," the BoJ said on its website.

BoJ Governor Kazuo Ueda told a news conference that it was "important to stabilise the underlying inflation rate", avoiding a situation in which it surpassed the two percent target with an "adverse impact on the economy".

Central bankers are keeping tabs on movements in the yen, which fell to a 40-year low against the dollar in July, prompting a historic joint US-Japanese intervention in foreign exchange markets.

The unit has been weighed in particular by the wide gap between Japan's still low interest rates and those of the Federal Reserve, which encouraged investors to favour better-yielding dollar-denominated assets.

Despite the hike to the highest level since 1995, which had been telegraphed for weeks, the yen weakened to more than 157 per dollar, compared with around 156.30 before the announcement.

"For a market looking for evidence that the BoJ could shorten the distance between hikes, those dissents mattered," said Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel.

"Traders were looking for signs that the Bank could move faster from here, yet two members were already arguing that even today's move had come too soon."

The cheap yen is driving up the cost of imported goods, which in turn is putting upward pressure on inflation.

Makiko Tsushima, a farmer from the northern region of Aomori, told AFP that she was "really wishing" for inflation to slow down.

"Prices are climbing. Casual shopping at a supermarket easily costs me 10,000 yen ($63) these days... Daily necessities like toilet paper and everything else are also expensive," the 54-year-old said.

Still, figures on Friday showed core inflation fell to 1.7 percent in August from 1.8 percent but remains close to the BoJ's two percent target.

articles.title: 5 key players in Congress on AI policy
articles.summary: Fears over artificial intelligence’s rapid development sent Congress into a tailspin this week, as dozens of lawmakers joined the debate on how to regulate the technology. The frenzy in Washington has included policymakers who have long engaged on the subject, but also those seizing on the mounting concerns for the first time. In the wake…
articles.body:
Fears over artificial intelligence’s rapid development sent Congress into a tailspin this week, as dozens of lawmakers joined the debate on how to regulate the technology.

The frenzy in Washington has included policymakers who have long engaged on the subject, but also those seizing on the mounting concerns for the first time.

In the wake of dire warnings from AI researchers, lawmakers floated around a range of ideas, from new caucuses and bills to classified briefings, while several older proposals got thrown back on the table.

While the prospect of passing AI safety legislation this year is low in Congress, a handful of lawmakers are expected to remain major voices on the issue on Capitol Hill.

Here are five key players to watch on AI policy:

Sanders is one of Congress’s biggest proponents of AI safety in Washington. He was one of the first policymakers to take up the cause of AI skeptics who believe the technology has existential risks to humanity, a concern that’s broken through the typical tech policy circles this month.

Over the past eight months, the Vermont progressive repeatedly called out AI’s risks to the workforce and its impact on consumer utility prices, along with the billionaire executives at the helm of these companies. He proposed some of the most drastic regulations on the technology, including a ban on the development of superintelligence or a moratorium on the data centers that power AI training and maintenance.

Most Democrats shied away from fully endorsing Sanders’s approach earlier this year as the party struggled to land on a consensus around the level of regulation for the technology. As Democrats tried to find their footing, Sanders became one of the loudest voices in Washington on the issue.

Sanders on Tuesday said Congress under both Democratic and Republican control “has been asleep at the wheel” on the issue while the decisions about AI development get made by “a handful of the richest people in the world.”

While most have not gone as far as Sanders on a solution, the panic following a warning from a former Anthropic researcher, Jacob Coxon, gave the lawmaker new momentum behind his safety approach.

Obernolte is one of the few lawmakers with a background in technology, holding both a bachelor’s degree in engineering and applied science and a master’s degree in AI.

His background, coupled with his willingness to work with the other side of the aisle and industry, made him a go-to voice on AI in Washington. When Congress was trying to understand the technology, Obernolte was tapped to chair the House Task Force on AI in 2024.

Since releasing a 275-page report on the task force’s research alongside Rep. Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) in 2024, Obernolte introduced several bills this Congress to address concerns around safety, American competitiveness and preemption.

This includes the bipartisan Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation and Reporting ( FRONTIER ) Act, which would establish requirements for AI firms like risk-management frameworks, independent audits and incident reporting. The bill, introduced with Rep. Lori Trahan (D-Mass.), would tier requirements based on the size of a firm.

As AI grows more politically divisive, the respect Obernolte has on the issue from his colleagues and industry and his work with Democrats put him on the map as someone who could bridge the gap in Congress.

Obernolte on Thursday told CNBC the FRONTIER Act “meets the moment and addresses safety concerns by balancing some light-touch regulation along with an environment we think will allow the beneficial uses of AI to flourish.”

“There’s nothing, frankly, about AI regulation that should be a partisan issue,” Obernolte said.

Like Obernolte, Trahan has made AI legislation a priority of her platform and is open to negotiations with Republicans.

The lawmakers’ FRONTIER Act was developed as part of their broader AI framework draft, the Great American AI Act, which put the Massachusetts Democrat in the spotlight on AI policy.

The nearly 300-page framework would preempt a limited set of state AI laws, aim to minimize AI risks and expand research on the technology. The discussion draft, which has not been formally introduced in the House, followed months of negotiations between the two parties and was described by industry observers as one of the most comprehensive bipartisan frameworks on AI.

Still, Trahan faced pushback from her own party over the draft at a time where Democrats were still figuring out their messaging on the issue.

Shortly after releasing the framework last June, the House Democratic Commission on AI and Innovation Economy said they could not support the discussion draft in its original form because it “does not meet the enormity of the moment.”

And the nonprofit AI safety group Americans for Responsible Innovation separately attacked Trahan in an ad stating, “AI oligarchs want to roll back civil rights and Rep. Lori Trahan is taking their side.”

Trahan suggested in an interview with WBUR this week that her colleagues are starting to catch on to the concerns she has had for months.

“I think my colleagues are scared,” she said, “They’re hearing from their constituents who want us to act. And this has been building since I started working on this issue this spring. This week has just hit a tipping point.”

Cruz will be crucial in steering which legislation moves through the Senate given his leadership of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation.

The Texas Republican does not fall into one camp on the issue, making him a potential wild card on AI regulations.

Following Coxon’s viral social media thread, Cruz said the researcher’s warnings were “scary as hell” and said “we need substantially more regulation when it comes to AI.”

But in the same interview with Politico, Cruz argued slowing down is an “impossible endeavor” because China will not “pause” on its own AI development, echoing rhetoric from other Republicans like President Trump and Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.).

“They are not going to stop,” Cruz said, adding, “This is somewhat tongue in cheek but it’s not entirely. If they’re going to be killer robots, I’d rather they be American killer robots and not Chinese killer robots.”

“The Chinese are putting no guardrails, they’re going full speed ahead,” he said.

Cruz is one of Congress’s most vocal critics of Big Tech, especially on kids’ online safety and antitrust. Earlier this week, he balked at Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei’s call for the government to provide a waiver to create an industry standard for safety with other companies.

Amodei, and other tech leaders like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, have suggested an industry standard in the wake of Congress’s inaction.

Unlike some on this list, Whitesides is a newer voice on the AI issue in the wake of Coxon’s warning, but he is standing out for his proposals .

In an interview with NewsNation’s Blake Burman on “The Hill” on Monday, the California Democrat said the U.S. needs a “safety stand-down” on AI for at least a month for all the companies.

Asked by Burman about what he meant by a “safety stand-down,” Whitesides replied that consumers’ everyday AI usage would continue but the “research on the frontier models, pushing forward that frontier, which is what people are scared about, would pause for a month while we do one thing.”

“We get the companies in the room, and we get experts, independent experts in the government, to talk about what are the red lines, what are the lines in the sand that we will not go past,” he continued. “We do not have that today. We need to have a common vision. And then Congress needs to work with those companies to put those red lines and lines in the sand into law.”

Whitesides, previously NASA’s chief of staff and the former CEO of Virgin Galactic, compared the “stand-down” approach to how the aerospace industry would temporarily stop launches after a serious flight accident to determine what went wrong.

He currently serves on the House Science, Space, and Technology and Armed Services committees.

articles.title: Intelligence community warned Congress on FISA 702 deadlines, but some Democrats have doubts
articles.summary: Trump administration intelligence officials are pressing Congress to renew the nation’s warrantless spy powers before Thanksgiving, warning they could run out of time to get a needed annual recertification for the program from the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC). Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) operates under dual authorities from Congress and…
articles.body:
Trump administration intelligence officials are pressing Congress to renew the nation’s warrantless spy powers before Thanksgiving, warning they could run out of time to get a needed annual recertification for the program from the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC).

Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) operates under dual authorities from Congress and the court, but the judicial backing for the spy tool that allows the government to spy on foreigners located abroad is set to expire in March.

Congress this year has repeatedly failed to renew FISA’s Section 702, and the spy program lapsed June 12 , entering uncharted territory by operating only under its court authorization.

In a meeting as Congress returned from summer break, staff from the office of the director of National Intelligence (ODNI) told lawmakers to pick up the pace, saying intelligence staff would need a few months to make their case for the program before the FISC.

But that’s sparked skepticism from some Democrats who want to see the law reformed, including by requiring a warrant to review any information inadvertently collected on Americans as the government conducts surveillance of its targets.

“They obviously just want to get it done because they know they’re going to lose the elections because they have fallen out of favor with the American people for good reason, and because they know they’re not going to be in control, they feel this is their chance to push FISA through without the privacy protections that America wants,” Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, told The Hill.

“So that’s a false deadline. March is the real deadline, and we need to get something done before that,” the congressman added.

The intelligence community is still able to conduct surveillance, in part because communications providers of cellphone and email services are cooperating with the requests and have not sued to question the legality of the program.

But the lapse in congressional reauthorization makes the March 17 court deadline all the more important.

Each year, the director of national intelligence and attorney general must seek certification of Section 702, laying out how they will conduct surveillance within the bounds of the law as laid out by Congress. That includes detailing procedures for screening out any information that might be collected on Americans and would also need to reflect any changes made by Congress in reauthorizing the powers.

First reported by Punchbowl News, ODNI staff stressed in meetings with congressional committees that the process before the FISC would take a few months, while House Intelligence Committee Chair Rick Crawford (R-Ark.) said first moves on that task would need to begin in December.

“The fact is, the courts have to recertify in December. Yes, the program is authorized till March, but they’ve got to recertify in December. If we don’t deliver something before that, it’s going to be complicated for them to implement the changes that we have in the FISA bill,” Crawford said.

“It does require significant lead time to be able to implement all that and go through the certification process. So this is not just simply saying, ‘Here it is and everything’s good’ — particularly when we have changes to the existing law.”

ODNI did not respond to a request for comment for this story.

FISA fault lines don’t fall cleanly along party lines, and one Democratic aide present for the meeting noted that GOP privacy hawks also pushed back against ODNI during the briefing.

But the staffer said the push on deadlines also comes as Democrats are feeling confident they will retake the House after the midterms.

Support for Section 702 has shrunk within the Democratic Party. While 147 Democrats voted to renew Section 702 in 2024, just 42 Democrats joined Republicans to back a House bill to renew 702 for three years that has since failed to be considered by the Senate.

“Our members are more skeptical of the Trump administration, but I think that skepticism is a bipartisan one. I think we’ve heard that from our members certainly behind closed doors from Democrats and Republicans,” the Democratic staffer said.

“I think that in the new Congress, the negotiations will be more fulsome, include more corners of our caucus and their conference, and yes, probably would involve additional checks on the intelligence community, and that ODNI has issued this warning, both because they really want it done and because they would rather take this deal than whatever deal we come up with.”

Not all Democrats want to punt the issue to the next Congress.

Rep. Jim Himes (D-Conn.) said the spy program is in a tenuous situation, essentially still functional only because tech companies chose not to sue when Section 702 failed to be reauthorized.

“The four or five people that I talked to that are pretty instrumental to reauthorizing this thing, nobody is trying to be too clever here, right? This process cannot expire, or we will be subject to some real evil. So at least I and others I think are thinking, ‘Let’s get this thing done on time,’” he told The Hill.

“We had a great development when the companies decided they weren’t going to sue and stop providing information. So let’s just get it done. Look, quite frankly, I would much rather we deal with it right now, both for temporal reasons, but also to have to do this under pressure with a brand new majority and a pissed off minority. That doesn’t feel smart to me.”

Hopes of passing a FISA 702 bill collapsed over the summer when President Trump installed Bill Pulte, the head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to temporarily lead ODNI.

Senators on both sides of the aisle revolted , noting Pulte’s history of forwarding Trump enemies for prosecution for mortgage fraud, but it was Democrats who refused to move forward on Section 702 until Pulte was out of the building.

Pulte has since been replaced by the now-confirmed Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, though the Senate has yet to take up its own Section 702 bill.

In the lower chamber, lawmakers who back Section 702 are eager to move on it.

“I was ready to get it done a while ago,” said Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio), chair of the House Judiciary Committee. “So hopefully we will.”

Crawford also vented frustration at the Senate.

“Well, they got the DNI [director of National Intelligence] confirmed. They got the one they wanted. Should be no further delays, no more excuses. And here we are. Probably won’t be back till sometime after [the] election, and they haven’t even dusted it off over there. So the House did their job. We passed that over here back in June. This is 100 percent on the Senate,” he said.

articles.title: China’s Fiscal Pullback Stretches Into August as Spending Slumps
articles.summary: China’s public expenditure declined at a quicker rate in August, indicating the government was still withdrawing fiscal support for the economy despite cooli...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- China's public expenditure declined at a quicker rate in August, indicating the government was still withdrawing fiscal support for the economy despite cooling growth momentum.

A measure of broad budget spending fell 6.7% last month from a year earlier, faster than its 4.4% drop in July, according to Bloomberg calculations based on Ministry of Finance data released on Friday. Broad revenue rose 2.9%.

As a result, the fiscal deficit shrank by a fifth in August, taking the shortfall in the first eight months of the year to 5.5 trillion yuan ($821 billion).

The deepening pullback in government spending partly explains the persistence of weak domestic demand in August, when consumption growth almost ground to a halt and investment continued to slump. Policymakers are likely keeping a close eye on how the economy fares in the next few weeks as they assess whether additional stimulus is needed to achieve their annual growth target of 4.5%-5%.

Officials have so far focused on the faster use of existing budget allocations instead of rolling out fresh supportive measures. In one such move, state-owned policy banks started deploying funding from a program that can unlock 800 billion yuan, mainly for infrastructure projects in 2026.

Government bonds slated to be issued during the rest of this year but still unsold were equivalent to around 1.1% of China's gross domestic product, according to estimates by Miao Yanliang, chief economist at China International Capital Corp. Authorities should be able to meet this year's growth target with spending financed by the borrowing, he said earlier this week.

articles.title: 119,000 fake shops could steal your credit card details
articles.summary: DoppelCart's 119,000 fake shopping domains steal credit card details at checkout, mimicking over 44,000 real brands with convincing cloned sites.
articles.body: You find a product you want for 65% off. The site looks polished, the branding feels familiar, and the deal seems hard to pass up. That could be exactly the trap. Cybersecurity company Nebty has linked about 119,000 domains to a fake shopping operation called DoppelCart. The sites impersonate legitimate businesses and can steal payment details at checkout, including one-time bank verification codes. BleepingComputer reports that more than 105,000 DoppelCart shops were active in Nebty's latest scans, while Nebty says the majority of the cluster remains online. So, before you jump on a huge discount from a store you do not recognize, take a closer look at who is really behind the checkout page. No technical experience is needed. Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com. What is DoppelCart? Nebty discovered DoppelCart while investigating fake shops that targeted several of its customers. Researchers noticed that stores impersonating different companies shared technical characteristics. They began following those connections through publicly available website scans. The investigation eventually grew to roughly 119,000 associated domains. Nebty says that, to its knowledge, DoppelCart represents the largest publicly documented fake-shop cluster when measured by associated domains. The company also makes an important point about attribution. Shared infrastructure does not prove that one person or organization controls every DoppelCart store. Even so, the technical overlap is striking. Nebty CEO Benedikt Scheungraber told BleepingComputer that 96% of the confirmed shops shared identical build files and resolved to 27 commerce backends. DoppelCart has swallowed a huge piece of the .shop domain Most of the domains connected to DoppelCart use the .shop top-level domain. Nebty's September 2026 data included 118,787 distinct .shop domains linked to the cluster out of 4,361,908 .shop domains in the company's snapshot. That's 2.72%, or roughly one out of every 37 domains in that particular data set. However, that number needs some context. Nebty says the snapshot represents domains listed in the .shop DNS zone. It does not tell us how many legitimate or fraudulent stores were operating at the same moment. For comparison, researchers previously documented BogusBazaar, a fake-shop operation involving more than 75,000 domains. Nebty cautions that observation periods and counting methods differ between investigations, so the numbers are not perfectly comparable. We reached out to GMO Registry, which operates the .shop domain, for comment but did not hear back before our deadline. Why DoppelCart fake shops can look so convincing The days when every scam website looked like somebody threw it together in five minutes are long gone. DoppelCart sites can copy product catalogs from real companies along with descriptions, branding and other material. In some cases, researchers found fake stores loading assets directly from the legitimate company's servers. That creates a real problem for shoppers. You may recognize the brand. The products look right. Nothing on the page immediately screams scam because much of the material came from the real business in the first place. Scheungraber says DoppelCart shops mimic 44,182 different brands, with a median of two clones for each brand. Some brands received much more attention. Researchers found more than 30 shops apiece targeting companies including SodaStream, Velasca, CurrentBody, Daniel Wellington, Dreame, Horze, MOVA and SPARK PAWS. That 65% discount can be the hook This is where the scam can catch you. Most of us shop around before spending money online. Finding the same product at a dramatically lower price can feel like a great deal. DoppelCart stores take advantage of that reaction. Researchers found fake shops advertising discounts as high as 65%. Of course, a steep discount does not automatically mean you're looking at a scam. Real stores run clearance sales every day. Still, if you've never heard of the retailer and its price beats everyone else by a mile, spend another minute checking who you're buying from. CyberGuy has a full guide on the warning signs worth checking before buying from an unfamiliar website: Tips to help you tell if an online store is real or a scam. 'THE ODYSSEY' STREAMING SCAM COULD STEAL YOUR BANK INFO How DoppelCart fake shops steal your card details The real danger starts when you decide to check out. Nebty tested several checkout pages tied to the DoppelCart cluster and found code collecting: According to the researchers, those fields can be transmitted through WebSockets to command-and-control infrastructure in real time. So, an attacker may receive the information while you're still sitting on the checkout page. The technique has similarities to web skimming, where malicious code captures payment information as a shopper types it into an online checkout page. We've previously broken down how that kind of attack works and why shoppers may see no obvious warning: Web skimming attacks target major payment networks. Your one-time bank code can be captured too This is the part I find especially concerning. Many of us have been trained to see a verification code from our bank as an extra layer of protection. DoppelCart can potentially turn that security step against you. Nebty found that the checkout code can relay the one-time confirmation code issued by a victim's bank. Attackers may then try to use the code to get past protections surrounding a fraudulent transaction. So, don't automatically enter a bank code simply because a checkout page asks for it. Read the bank's message carefully. Look at the merchant and transaction details if they're included. If something does not match the purchase you're making, stop the transaction and contact your bank through its official app or the number printed on your card. The legitimate business can get dragged into the scam DoppelCart creates another headache after the purchase. Some fake shops display the real company's legitimate customer support address. Now imagine you place an order and nothing arrives. You find the support information on the site and contact the business demanding to know where your purchase went. The company you're calling may have no idea what you're talking about because you never bought anything from it. Nebty says legitimate businesses have received complaints from shoppers over orders those businesses never processed. The scammer gets the payment information. Meanwhile, the legitimate company gets the angry customer and has to explain that somebody copied its store. Nebty says it tried to contact the main hosting provider associated with DoppelCart sites but received no response. Want to see whether a brand or website appears in the DoppelCart investigation? Search Nebty's DoppelCart database at investigations.nebty-id.com/doppelcart. APPLE PAY TEXT SCAM THREATENS $8,250 LOSS IN 35 MINUTES How to spot a fake online store before you pay A professional-looking site no longer gives you enough information to decide whether a retailer deserves your trust. Instead, slow down when you're shopping somewhere unfamiliar. 1) Check the exact web address Look at the domain in your browser before entering payment information. A fake site may use a recognizable company name inside a completely different domain. If you're trying to buy directly from a well-known brand, find its official website independently. Also, don't let the padlock or HTTPS fool you. HTTPS tells you a website encrypts the connection. It does not prove the seller behind the site is legitimate. Scammers can encrypt websites too. 2) Take another look at an extreme discount A 65% discount can make you want to buy before the deal disappears. That's when I would slow down. Check the product on the company's official website or compare it with a retailer you already know. If the price difference looks unusually large, investigate the seller. 3) Research an unfamiliar retailer Search the store's name before buying. Look beyond reviews displayed on the website itself. Search for independent complaints or reports that connect the domain to scams. Then check the company's contact information. A cloned website can look impressive while having very little legitimate history behind it. 4) Pay by credit card when possible The Federal Trade Commission recommends paying by credit card when possible for online purchases because credit cards provide protections when a transaction goes wrong. Some issuers also let you use virtual card numbers for online purchases. Availability varies by issuer. A virtual number can keep your primary card number away from the merchant and may let you shut down the virtual number if something goes wrong. 5) Read bank verification messages carefully Don't treat a one-time verification code as a routine box to fill in. Read the message your bank sends. If the merchant or transaction looks unfamiliar, do not enter the code. Contact your card issuer through a trusted channel instead. 6) Turn on transaction alerts Check whether your bank or card issuer lets you receive notifications when purchases hit your account. Alerts can help you spot an unfamiliar transaction quickly. Do not ignore a small charge simply because the amount looks harmless. Any transaction you don't recognize deserves a closer look. 7) Use strong security software Strong antivirus software can help warn you about known malicious websites and dangerous links. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com However, no program catches every newly created fake shopping site. That means your own judgment still plays an important role when a store you've never heard of suddenly offers the deal of the year. What to do if you already entered your card on a suspicious shop Act quickly if you think you purchased from a DoppelCart site or another fake retailer. The FTC recommends contacting the financial institution you used to make the payment as soon as possible. Contact your card issuer right away Use the number on the back of your card, your bank's official app or its official website. Tell the issuer that you entered your card information on a suspected fraudulent website. Ask whether the card should be locked or replaced with a new number. If you also entered a one-time verification code from your bank, tell them that too. Check your account for suspicious charges Review your recent transactions and continue watching the account. If you paid the fake retailer, tell your issuer that you believe the transaction involved a scam. Also report any other charges you do not recognize. The FTC recommends asking the card issuer or bank whether it can reverse the fraudulent transaction and return your money. Change any password you reused If the fake store asked you to create an account and you reused a password from somewhere else, change that password on the other accounts. Give important accounts unique passwords. A password manager can help generate and store strong passwords without forcing you to remember every one. Watch for follow-up scams Remember what DoppelCart checkout pages can collect. The people behind the operation may have your contact information along with payment details. Be suspicious of unexpected bank warnings, delivery messages or refund offers connected to the purchase. Scammers sometimes target people who already lost money and then pose as someone who can help recover it. Go directly to your bank or the company's official website rather than clicking a link in an unexpected message. Run a security scan if you downloaded something If you downloaded a file, installed software or gave the suspicious site additional access to your device, update your security software and run a scan with strong antivirus software. If all you did was type card information into the fake checkout, focus first on protecting the payment account and watching for fraudulent transactions. Report the fake store Report suspected fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Reports can help authorities identify fraud patterns and investigate scam operations. Kurt's key takeaways What bothers me most about DoppelCart is how convincing these fake stores can look. You may recognize the products and the branding because scammers copied them from a real business. For me, that changes how I look at a bargain from a store I don't know. If the price seems unusually low, I want to know exactly who I'm buying from before I enter my card information. Take a minute to check the web address and search for the retailer on your own. That small pause could save you from having to replace your card or deal with fraudulent charges later. articles.title: Paris prosecutors are investigating smart glasses-enabled sexual harassment.
articles.summary:
They’ve opened “at least one criminal probe” following complaints about the glasses being used to film women on the street in public without their consent, Reuters reports. France’s data protection authority also says businesses are “increasingly” asking if they can ban smart glasses at work, similar to a ban under consideration in Australia.
